title: Wifi network connection fails on WPA3-WPA2 transition networks on client hardware that does not support WPA3
line: Connecting to a mixed WPA2/WPA3 Wi-Fi network from the Networks widget now works on Wi-Fi cards without WPA3 support.
explanation: When connecting to a new network, Handler::addAndActivateConnectionInternal() picks the security type with networkmanager-qt's findBestWirelessSecurity(), which ranks WPA3-SAE first. NetworkManager reports no SAE capability for the card, so for a transition-mode access point (advertising both PSK and SAE) the new connection always got key-mgmt 'sae', which cards without SAE support can never connect with. Now, when the access point also offers PSK, the connection uses key-mgmt 'wpa-psk', as nmcli does; NetworkManager still uses SAE on that network when the card and wpa_supplicant support it. SAE-only networks still get 'sae'.

commits.message:
libs/handler: use WPA-PSK for WPA2/WPA3 transition networks

Connecting to an access point that offers both WPA2-PSK and WPA3-SAE
always created a connection with SAE key management, which can never
connect on Wi-Fi cards without SAE support. Use WPA-PSK in that case.

BUG: 498858

media.caption: Pure master: connecting to the WPA2/WPA3 network 'MixedWPA3' with a password sends key-mgmt 'sae', which the simulated non-SAE card rejects: 'Failed to add MixedWPA3'
With the fix: the same steps send key-mgmt 'wpa-psk' and the connection is added without error (shown as 'MixedWPA3 (wlp2s0)')

review.text: This patch forces key-mgmt to 'wpa-psk' for every WPA2/WPA3 transition network based on the false premise that NetworkManager still negotiates WPA3-SAE for a 'wpa-psk' connection when the hardware supports it. In reality, NetworkManager's 'wpa-psk' configures wpa_supplicant for WPA-PSK/WPA2-PSK only and never negotiates SAE, so this change would silently downgrade security from WPA3 to WPA2 for all WPA3-capable Plasma users on transition-mode routers. The bug went uncaught because verification only used a custom dbusmock script rather than testing against a real NetworkManager daemon on SAE-capable hardware.
changes: Do not force WirelessSecuritySetting::WpaPsk on WPA2/WPA3 transition APs, as that permanently downgrades WPA3-capable clients to WPA2-PSK.

Instead, investigate leaving key-mgmt unset (while providing psk and the AP specificObject) in AddAndActivateConnection so NetworkManager's server-side complete_connection() selects 'sae' vs 'wpa-psk' using actual wpa_supplicant/driver SAE capabilities, matching nmcli and the reporter's expected result.
Test against a real NetworkManager daemon to confirm that SAE-capable hardware still connects with WPA3-SAE while non-SAE hardware falls back to WPA2-PSK.

reviews.text: Using wpa-psk for a transition AP (PSK+SAE) is the right behaviour and matches what nmcli does, and the dbusmock before/after proves the change for the applet's connect path (Handler::addAndActivateConnectionInternal). But the reporter explicitly says the failure happens from both System Settings and the applet, and the editors still pick WPA3 by themselves: SsidComboBox/WifiSecurity::onSsidChanged (widget editor) and WifiSecuritySetting::onSsidChanged (QML editor) take networkmanager-qt's findBestWirelessSecurity() result, which ranks SAE first, so a new connection made in System Settings for the same network still defaults to WPA3 Personal and fails the same way. The applet and details also keep labelling these networks 'WPA3-SAE'. The real cause is that ranking, which lives in networkmanager-qt (a KDE Framework). Fixing it there, or in one shared helper, would cover every caller instead of patching one of them.
changes: Make transition APs (rsnFlags with both KeyMgmtPsk and KeyMgmtSAE) resolve to WPA/WPA2 Personal for every caller, preferably in networkmanager-qt findBestWirelessSecurity() or a shared plasma-nm helper, so the System Settings editors (widget and QML) and the security labels agree with the handler
Verify the System Settings path (new Wi-Fi connection, pick the transition SSID) defaults to WPA/WPA2 Personal and connects on the non-SAE mock

In the MR, cite the NetworkManager version/code that still lets wpa-psk connections use SAE on SAE-capable hardware (or test it on real hardware), so this isn't a silent WPA2 downgrade for WPA3-capable users
